claims.text: The matrix tool's summary label is corrected from '*** NEVER — DECORATIVE ***' to '*** NEVER OBSERVED FAILING — MAY BE UNTESTED ***', with a footer stating that before calling any control decorative you must confirm a mutation aimed at ITS subject ran to completion and the control still passed. The tool also now distinguishes a mutation that CRASHED the subject — which tests nothing — from one that ran and went uncaught.

The label misled me three times in a single exercise, each time toward accusing another arm's work of being decorative: six controls when two mutation anchors silently failed to apply; the no-chain control when M8 crashed the subject before any verdict was rendered; and the summary count read as a finding rather than as a gap in my own coverage. None of the three was a real defect in Prime's suite.

The cited copy at AR_matrix_completed/ctl_matrix.py was NOT edited. CHECKPOINT-06 still ADMITS at exit 0. The corrected tool is a new file at a new path, fleet_state/arms/ARM-06/tools/, per the frozen-hash rule — the historical artifact records what the tool was when its findings were published, and the corrected one is what anyone should run next.

tests.command: python3 -c 'ast.parse(...)'  # corrected tool parses; AR envelope re-validated

risks: I corrected the WORDING and the crash-detection. I did not make the tool refuse to summarise — a reader who ignores the footer can still misread the table exactly as I did. Wording is a weaker fix than structure, and I am not claiming it prevents the error, only that it stops asserting the false one.
The corrected tool has not been exercised against a fresh matrix run. It parses and the label is present; that is not the same as having watched it report correctly on a mutation that crashes.
